seo.title: HubGet vs Winstall.app – comparison
seo.description: HubGet vs Winstall.app: a desktop app that installs, updates and uninstalls apps from WinGet, Chocolatey and Scoop, or a web-based WinGet command generator?
seo.ogDescription: A desktop app store for Windows, or a web-based WinGet command generator? A feature comparison of HubGet and Winstall.app.

texty.t5: Both tools save you from hunting for installers on the web, and both are built on WinGet. Winstall.app is a website that puts together a command for your terminal. HubGet is a desktop app store that installs apps for you, keeps track of their updates and can uninstall them too.
texty.t21: Copy and run in a terminal
texty.t25: In the app vs in a terminal
texty.t37: {info}A desktop app for Windows 10 and 11 with a Windows 11-style window
texty.t38: {info}A website that runs in your browser
texty.t40: {partly}HubGet – an installer of about 6 MB that doesn’t need admin rights
texty.t41: {yes}Nothing – just a browser and WinGet, which comes with Windows 10 and 11
texty.t43: {yes}WinGet, Chocolatey and Scoop in one catalog – more than 25,000 apps. An app from several sources has a single card
texty.t46: {yes}One click right in the app – an operation queue and download progress in percent
texty.t47: {partly}Generates a command or a .bat / .ps1 script that you copy and run in a terminal
texty.t49: {yes}An overview of installed apps (including those outside WinGet, Microsoft Store apps and Steam games), “Update all” and uninstall
texty.t50: {no}Out of scope – it’s for putting together an install command
texty.t52: {yes}Scheduled checks and installs at a set time, notifications, a minimum age for updates and exceptions for battery and metered connections
texty.t53: {no}No – you run update commands in the terminal yourself
texty.t55: {yes}Finds leftovers in AppData, Program Files, the Start menu and the registry and offers to delete them. With install tracking, it knows everything the installer created
texty.t57: Chocolatey and Scoop in the app
texty.t58: {yes}Install, update and uninstall right in the app – plus a fallback source when WinGet fails
texty.t61: {yes}When WinGet reports a broken download link, HubGet automatically tries Chocolatey and then Scoop
texty.t64: {yes}A banner in the icon’s colors, a screenshot gallery (for ~2,500 apps), SHA-256, dependencies and terminal commands
texty.t65: {partly}An app page with a description, links and the install command
texty.t67: {yes}Average star rating, rating breakdown and the most helpful reviews – add your own after signing in with GitHub
texty.t70: {yes}Package bundles with import and export (.ubundle, PowerShell script, WinGet export)
texty.t71: {yes}Collections (“packs”) shared via a link, plus script export
texty.t73: {yes}A tray icon – installs finish even after you close the window
texty.t74: {no}Installs run in a terminal you start yourself
texty.t76: {yes}Everything that starts when you sign in to Windows, in one place – turn items on or off with one click and see their impact on startup
texty.t80: {yes}Prepare the list and command in any browser, even on another device
texty.t89: Each one fits a different job.
texty.t90: {ikona} HubGet is a good fit if you…
texty.t91: want to install, update and uninstall apps without a terminal
texty.t92: want an overview of every app on your PC and its updates
texty.t93: want to pick from WinGet, Chocolatey and Scoop in one place
texty.t94: are setting up a new PC and want it ready with your own bundle of apps in minutes
texty.t95: Winstall.app is a good fit if you…
texty.t96: don’t want to install anything and a browser is enough
texty.t97: are preparing a command or script for another PC or for automation
texty.t98: only use WinGet and are comfortable in a terminal
texty.t101: Is HubGet a good alternative to Winstall.app?
texty.t102: Yes, if you want to manage apps right in Windows. Winstall.app helps you pick apps and put together a command that you then run in a terminal. HubGet installs the apps itself, shows their progress, keeps track of updates and can uninstall them too – and besides WinGet, its catalog also covers Chocolatey and Scoop.
texty.t103: Can I switch from Winstall.app to HubGet?
texty.t104: Yes. Both tools are built on the same WinGet repository, so the apps from your collections are in the HubGet catalog too. Just search for them and save them to your own package bundle – then install it all at once or export it as a PowerShell script.
texty.t105: Can HubGet install from Chocolatey and Scoop?
texty.t106: Yes. HubGet installs, updates and uninstalls apps from Chocolatey and Scoop right in the app. Both managers also serve as a fallback source when WinGet has a broken download link.
texty.t108: Yes. HubGet is open source under the MIT license, free and without ads. Winstall.app is free too, and its source code is published under the GPL-3.0 license.
texty.t110: Free, open source and ad-free. The installer is about 6 MB and doesn’t need admin rights.
